messages:
Elena R: FYI — FarmWave (acct fw-882) reported an ACH return for invoice INV-2026-09. Bank return code: R02 (Invalid routing number). Provider tx: pay_0x9a12. Customer says their routing is 021000021 but our payout shows 21000021. Can someone confirm if we strip leading zeros anywhere?

Billing Bot: automatic update — invoice INV-2026-09 status: payment_returned, return_code: R02, amount: $14,250.

Kevin Patel: Can you paste the exact payload we sent to the payments provider (raw) + provider transaction id? Need to reproduce.

Elena R: Pasting the request we sent to provider (sanitized):
```json
{
  "provider_tx": "pay_0x9a12",
  "reference": "INV-2026-09",
  "amount": 14250,
  "currency": "USD",
  "payment_method": "ach",
  "bank_account": {
    "account_number": "123456789",
    "routing_number": "21000021",
    "bank_name": "FirstState Bank",
    "account_holder": "FarmWave LLC"
  }
}
```
Note routing_number above is what ended up in the request (no leading zero).

Ops Oncall: I pulled logs for payments-transform between 2026-05-19T14:12:30Z and 2026-05-19T14:13:10Z. Found this transform log: 
```
INFO payments-transform v1.14.2 format_routing - input_routing=021000021 output_routing=21000021 transform=strip_leading_zeros
```
Looks like we intentionally stripped zeros during normalization there.

Kevin Patel: That log confirms it — bug is in payments-transform v1.14.2. We used an int-cast / lstrip('0') somewhere in the formatting step. Repro steps: run the formatter locally and POST a payload: 
```
curl -s -X POST "https://payments.internal/v1/format" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"routing_number":"021000021","account_number":"123456789"}'
# -> {"routing_number":"21000021"}
```
So our formatter is dropping the leading zero.

Maria Gonzales: If we need to reissue, the customer requires the original PO (PO#55023) on the updated invoice before their AP will accept. Also, do we need to wait for bank clearing on returned funds or can we do a fresh debit?

Kevin Patel: We can retry a new payout now with the corrected routing. Providers usually require a fresh transfer (cannot reuse provider tx id). I opened PR #1128 to keep leading zeros and avoid numeric coercion. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/payments/pull/1128

deploy-bot: Deploy started for payments-transform hotfix (PR #1128) to canary-us-east.

Kevin Patel: Hotfix merged. Canary deployed. Changed formatting to treat routing as string and preserve leading zeros. Please run manual retry for pay_0x9a12 with routing "021000021" (new attempt id payment_retry_1843127920).

Billing Bot: Manual retry scheduled: payment_retry_1843127920 status: pending.

Sofia Chen: I'll ping FarmWave and ask them to confirm their bank trace number once the retry goes through. Also they asked us to add PO#55023 onto the updated invoice — cc @Maria Gonzales.

Elena R: Provider reports retry accepted and settled. FarmWave confirms funds received. Closing internal ticket TICK-4312. Thanks team! :tada: :heart:

Kevin Patel: Follow-up: added a unit test to prevent routing normalization regressions and rolled the change to prod us-east-1. Will schedule backport to older branches.

Maria Gonzales: I'll issue the updated invoice with PO#55023 and mark the payment reconciled.

Elena R: Excellent. Noting root cause = payments-transform stripping leading zeros on routing numbers. Logging here for the billing/escalation thread.
